title: The Agent in the Middle: How AI-Mediated Access Reshapes Web Vulnerability Exploitation
abstract: arXiv:2610.35541v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Web services increasingly expose backend interfaces that let users delegate tasks to AI agents, which invoke service operations directly without navigating websites. This shift changes how existing Web vulnerabilities can be exploited. We investigate these changes through VELA, an executable benchmark covering 44 vulnerabilities across twelve Web application families. The benchmark preserves vulnerable backends and derives agent-facing interfaces from legitimate workflows. We evaluate three commercial agents across multiple interface configurations, using controlled comparisons to separate interface effects from agent behavior and independent oracles to verify attack outcomes. Our results show that the agent realizes every attack that direct interface invocation realizes in the reference configuration, so exploitability is set mainly by the interface: 91% of vulnerabilities remain exploitable under the reference design. translated_title: 中间的智能体：AI中介访问如何重塑Web漏洞利用
translated_abstract: Web服务越来越多地暴露后端接口，允许用户将任务委托给AI智能体，这些智能体无需浏览网站即可直接调用服务操作。这种转变改变了现有Web漏洞被利用的方式。我们通过VELA来研究这些变化，VELA是一个可执行的基准测试，涵盖十二个Web应用家族中的44个漏洞。该基准保留了存在漏洞的后端，并从合法工作流中推导出面向智能体的接口。我们在多种接口配置下评估了三个商业智能体，使用受控比较来区分接口效应与智能体行为，并使用独立的判定标准来验证攻击结果。我们的结果表明，在参考配置下，智能体能够实现直接接口调用所能实现的所有攻击，因此可利用性主要由接口决定：在参考设计下，91%的漏洞仍然可被利用。
tldr: 提出可执行基准测试VELA，系统研究了AI智能体中介访问对Web漏洞利用的影响，发现面向智能体的接口设计决定了漏洞可利用性，参考设计下91%的漏洞仍然可被利用。
en_tdlr: Introduces VELA, an executable benchmark demonstrating that AI-mediated agent access preserves 91% of Web vulnerability exploitability, with exploitability primarily determined by the agent-facing interface design rather than agent behavior.
